summary: Sketch dimensions on the canvas are now selected before they are edited. Hovering a dimension's value, line or arrows highlights the points, lines, arcs and circles it measures; hovering a row in the relations or constraint issues list highlights the same geometry, including the origin or axis that a coordinate is measured from. A click selects one dimension and replaces the geometry selection, Shift toggles, Escape clears, and the status line names the selection. Double-click or Enter opens the existing editor; Space selects. Opening the editor, also from Edit value…, keeps the dimension selected and leaves the geometry unselected, so Delete removes the dimension, never the geometry it measures, while the editor is open and after Apply or Cancel. The editor selects only the dimension it edits. In the relations list, also when it opens from a point's or curve's Constraints and dimensions or Dimension menu, opening a dimension's row makes that dimension the selection, so switching rows moves the selection, and opening another relation's row returns the selection to the geometry the list belongs to. The editor belongs to its part, sketch and dimension: it closes when geometry, the sketch origin or an axis, a profile or another dimension takes the selection, or when another part opens under the same IDs, and selecting a dimension clears the origin and axes. Cancel closes the editor for good: a later Escape, or an edit that remounts the relations list, never reopens or focuses it, and a row closed in the list stays closed. Delete or Backspace removes the selected dimensions in one undo step through the same prepared edit as the relations list, and a refused removal keeps them with its message. Keyboard focus never changes the selection, so Tab moves through dimensions, points and edges without closing an editor: Delete or Backspace on a focused dimension label or profile chip, and Delete on a focused point or edge, remove the current selection, what is drawn selected, and the focused item only while nothing is selected; Backspace removes only dimensions, and with the origin, an axis or a legacy profile selected a focused label removes nothing. Point to line distances, also those measured from an arc or circle center, select, edit, highlight their point and line, convert with Make reference and Make driving and delete like the other dimensions. A right-click menu offers Edit value…, Make reference or Make driving, and Delete; commands that do not apply stay visible, disabled, with the reason. Dimensions draw thinner: no label box, 1 px lines, slimmer arrows, quieter extension lines and haloed monospace values in theme colours, with reference values in parentheses and a dimmer colour; a selected dimension keeps the selection colour while hovered or focused, and keyboard focus underlines its value. Dimension lines and arrows lie beneath the sketch: where one crosses or ends on a point, line, arc or circle, the sketch origin or an axis, or a profile grip or edge, that geometry keeps the hover, click, Shift-click, double-click, right-click, drag and box selection start, and a right-click there offers the geometry under it before the dimension menu. Construction edges take the pointer along their whole length, also in the gaps of their dashes, so a dimension beneath never takes a press there. The value label stays above the geometry, extension lines never take the pointer, a dimension hover ends when the window loses focus, and away from geometry a dimension's line and arrows select, edit and open the menu of their dimension. Dimension hover and selection highlights draw above the fully defined, conflicting and redundant geometry colours, and a definition lock refuses only moves: dimensions on fully defined geometry, and that geometry itself, select, take focus and delete as on free geometry. A selection, keyboard focus and an open menu belong to the dimension they were made on: a new value, Make reference and Make driving keep it selected, also when the driver is stored on a point that a Coincident relation joins to the measured point in the sketch after the change, so an edit, undo or redo that also removes that relation drops the selection and one that adds it keeps it, and so does a Trim or Extend that moves an end of a referenced line; a dimension that undo, redo or an agent edit removes, or replaces with another measurement under the same ID, comes back unselected and without focus, a closing menu or editor does not return focus to the replacement, and a menu closes without running a command when the sketch changes or the edit is cancelled. The size chips on older and plugin profiles draw as plain haloed values like the canvas dimensions, through a new shared annotation button appearance, and follow the same rules: a click selects and highlights the leader, double-click or Enter edits and selects only the chip it edits, opening another part closes a chip editor and clears the chip selection, Delete removes a driving dimension, and the menu offers Edit value…, a disabled Make reference with its reason, and Delete. Accessible names change: canvas dimensions read Dimension or Reference dimension, the quantity and value, then press Enter to edit, instead of Configure or Inspect reference; profile chips read Dimension, the quantity and value, then press Enter to edit, instead of Edit and the quantity.
warning: Potentially breaking for automation and people that click a dimension expecting its editor: a click now only selects, and a double-click or Enter opens the editor. Automation that finds a canvas dimension by its accessible name must use the new names, for example Dimension distance 15 mm, press Enter to edit instead of Configure distance 15 mm, and Reference dimension diameter 6 mm, press Enter to edit instead of Inspect reference diameter 6 mm. Profile size chips change from Edit Width to Dimension width 30 mm, press Enter to edit. Delete with a dimension selected removes the dimension, not geometry. Delete on a focused point, edge, dimension label or profile chip now removes the current selection when something else is selected, where it used to remove the focused item, and Backspace on a focused dimension label with geometry selected removes nothing; automation that focused an item to delete it must select it first. While the editor of a canvas dimension is open, cad_get_viewport.selectedSketchGeometrySet is empty: opening the editor by double-click, Enter or Edit value… keeps the dimension selected instead of selecting the geometry it measures, so automation that read the edited geometry from the viewport selection must read the relation from the document instead. The same applies when a dimension's row is opened in the relations list, including a list opened from a geometry's Constraints and dimensions or Dimension menu: that dimension becomes the selection and selectedSketchGeometrySet empties, and opening a relation that is not a dimension restores the geometry. Opening an editor on one of several selected dimensions or chips selects that one alone, and an open dimension editor closes when a legacy profile, the sketch origin or an axis is selected or another part opens. No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD documents or controller output.

checklist.schema: No CAD schema change: removals use the existing remove-sketch-relation and remove-sketch-dimension edits, and conversions use set-sketch-relation with the existing reference-dimension, distance, point-line-distance and radial-size kinds. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol change; the Rust solver and committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. Hover runs no solver or analysis call and renders only the highlight overlay, which draws after the point and edge rows so the definition colours never cover it; moving the pointer across a dimension label, line or arrow, or across relation and issue rows, does not render the sketch canvas. The wider line and arrow targets that take the pointer sit in a layer drawn before the point and edge rows, so the browser's own hit test gives the geometry the pointer. The origin, axes, profile grips and profile edges are not rows: on a line, one cover test per pointer event asks the grip, datum and profile edge pickers once each and never searches the sketch graph, and the canvas hover for that event reuses its answer. The transparent hit stroke of a construction edge is continuous while its drawn stroke stays dashed. Hover over a line marks its dimension with a class, without rendering the dimension layer, and a window blur drops that mark and the hover highlight, and a right-click on a line or arrow offers the geometry under it in the overlap chooser before the dimension menu. Canvas and chip menus close, and their commands are dropped, when the part, version, build or sketch changed, the edit was cancelled, or the dimension was replaced after the menu opened. Selections keep the dimension identity they were made on, so a reused relation or constraint ID never inherits one. Keyboard focus is bound to the same identity: a replacement under the same ID mounts a new label or chip, so neither focus nor a closing menu or editor returns to it, and Delete, Backspace and menu commands check the identity before they run. A line-length reference is identified by its line, so a Trim or Extend that rewrites an endpoint keeps it selected. A canvas dimension editor records the part identity, sketch and dimension it belongs to, and closes in the same render once the selection is anything but that dimension alone or the part identity changes; the relations panel reports the row it edits, so the selection follows a row switch, and a closed row is recorded in the command, so a remounted panel keeps it closed. Cancel drops the open relations command, so neither a later Escape nor a remount focuses a cancelled editor, and another part or sketch clears the selection during render, before a relations row can mount or take focus in it. A selection stores its dimension's measurement as authored: point IDs, line ID and quantity. A successor of the same form is compared by that authored identity; one of another form is compared by resolving both measurements through the Coincident relations of the current sketch, with the point identities cached per sketch graph, so a conversion that stores the measurement on the joined point keeps the selection, and an edit, undo or redo that also removes or adds the join is judged by the sketch after it. Only Coincident relations join points, and a measurement that differs drops the selection and closes the editor. A relations or issue row's highlight follows its row after every panel render: it is drawn again from the current draft while the row is listed, and hidden when an edit removes the row or remounts it with the focus that showed it; a profile chip's leader hover goes with the chip's key, so a replacement constraint is not drawn hovered. Keyboard focus never moves the selection: Delete and Backspace on a focused label, chip, point or edge act on the selection, which menus select on opening. Profile chip editors close when the part identity changes. WebMCP tools and their arguments are unchanged, and dimension selection is not part of the agent viewport state. One viewport value changes: cad_get_viewport.selectedSketchGeometrySet is empty while a canvas dimension editor is open, including one opened from the relations list, where it used to hold the measured geometry; docs/site/agents.md says so.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. Canvas dimensions and profile chips gain selection, hover highlight, Delete and a context menu; double-click or Enter opens the editor that a click opened before. Opening that editor, from the canvas, a relations list row or a geometry menu, no longer selects the measured geometry: the editor works on it while the dimension alone is selected. Point to line distances gain Make reference and Make driving from the canvas menu, using the existing point-line-distance reference measurement and keeping the side the point is on. The shared Button gains an annotation variant and theme.css gains the --annotation-halo token; existing variants are unchanged.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved documents open unchanged and older releases open documents edited with this one.
checklist.verification: Full Vitest passed after the round 9 fix, on the merge of main at 0.0.779: 556 files, 6377 tests. cadSketchDimensionSelection unit tests cover selection, the dimension identity rules (value edits, Make reference and Make driving keep a pick; a reused ID that measures something else drops it; a line reference keeps its pick when Trim or Extend rewrites an endpoint and through a later Make driving), refreshed picks, mount keys that change only on replacement, reconciliation, status text, highlight targets and the hover store; CadSketchGraphDimensions, CadSketchCanvasRender, CadSketchDimensionControls, CadGearInteraction and CadWorkbench tests cover click selection, Shift toggles, Space, Escape, Enter and double-click editing, hover highlights from labels and relation rows, one-step Delete, refused removal messages, the context menu with disabled reasons, menus that close on a replaced dimension, a part change or Cancel, selections that never pass to a reused ID, that pointer moves across labels, dimension lines, arrows, relation rows and issue rows render only the overlay, that Enter, double-click and Edit value… keep the dimension selected with no geometry selected so Delete removes only the dimension before and after Apply and Cancel, that focus, a closing menu or editor, and a right-press never pass to a replacement label or chip, that a relations row switch, a geometry menu's Constraints and dimensions or Dimension, and a non-dimension row move the selection with the edited row, that an editor opened on one of several selected dimensions or chips selects it alone, and that a legacy profile selection or another part under the same IDs closes a canvas or chip dimension editor. Round 4 tests check that Delete and Backspace on a focused label, chip, point or edge remove the selection and the focused item only while nothing is selected, that Escape after Cancel never focuses or reopens a cancelled editor, for an existing and a new dimension, that a closed row stays closed when an edit remounts the relations list, and that a non-dimension row never takes focus in another part. After the merge, a point to line distance made by the circle double-pick selects, edits on its center and line, highlights both, converts with Make reference and Make driving and deletes, and a datum selection and a dimension selection replace each other, an axis closes an open editor and a focused label deletes nothing past a selected axis. Round 5 tests check that a length stored on a coincident alias of a line's endpoint, and a point to line distance stored on an alias of its point, stay selected when the relations list makes them references on the line and on the measured point and through Make driving, while another line, another point, a point that only lies on the measured one or the same edit without the Coincident relation drops the selection, and that a line reference keeps its pick through a Trim and a later driver on the new end's alias; a Chromium computed-style check confirms that a selected driving or reference label and a selected profile chip keep the selection colour while hovered or focused, that hover and focus still brighten an unselected label, and that focus keeps the underline or focus ring. Round 6 tests check, for a length and for a point to line distance, that one edit that converts the selected dimension and removes the Coincident relation it is measured through drops the selection, renews its key and selects the successor afresh, that one that adds the relation keeps the selection and its key, that Delete afterwards removes only what is selected, and that undo and redo across either edit keep the selection only in the sketch where the dimension still measures the same points. After the merge with 0.0.779, a test checks that a dimension on fully defined geometry selects and highlights above the definition colours with the marks kept, that focus on a defined point leaves the selection, that Delete on a focused defined point removes the selected dimension, the selected point or, with nothing selected, the focused point, and that pressing a defined point selects it; the render tests check that hover renders only the highlight overlay and that definition changes render only the changed rows. Round 7 tests check that a focused or hovered relation row, and a hovered issue row, that an outside edit removes without a blur or pointer leave hide their highlight; that an outside edit that changes a row's operands redraws a hovered row's highlight from the current draft and hides a focused row's, whose focus the panel reset takes; that Make driving in the panel redraws the highlight of the row that stays focused or hovered; and that a hovered profile chip replaced under the same field loses its leader highlight while a value change keeps it. Round 8 tests check, in Chromium, that a point and a circle's edge under a radius dimension's line and arrow keep the hover, click, double-click, right-click and drag, that Shift-click there adds to the selection, that a box starts there with the points and with the edges filter, and that the line between them selects the radius, opens its menu and edits it; in jsdom, that the line targets lie beneath the rows and the labels above them, that a line and its arrows select, toggle, edit and open the menu away from geometry and datums, that an axis under a line keeps the hover, click, Shift-click, double-click and right-click, and that a right-click at an arrow tip offers the edge before the dimension; and a render test that hover along a line and across the axis under it asks the grip and profile edge pickers once per move, never the graph, and renders neither rows nor dimensions. Each round 2 to 8 test, and each merge test, fails with its fix reverted: with the round 6 fix reverted all eight round 6 tests fail, and so do mutations that skip the Coincident joins, share one resolver between graphs, compare keys or reconciliation without the current graph, or identify a line reference by its ID alone. With the round 8 fix reverted the four round 8 jsdom tests, the new Chromium test and cad-sketch-arc-trim fail, as on CI. Drawing the line targets above the rows fails the layer order test and the Chromium test, and with the dimension menu also before the overlap chooser every hover, click, double-click, right-click, drag, Shift-click and box start step of that test fails for both the point and the edge. Mutations that let nothing cover a line, or that ignore the cover on hover, press or right-press, fail the axis test; one that opens the dimension menu before the overlap chooser fails the arrow tip test; and keeping the line hover in React state, dropping the per-event cover or making the canvas hover ignore it fail the render test. tsc -b, npm run build, npm run lint, npm run ui:check, npm run docs:check and node scripts/check-release.mjs origin/main pass. agent-file-import, which timed out after a reload on CI, is not slower on this branch: three single runs with --workers=2 took 6.7, 6.6 and 7.5 s against 6.8, 6.5 and 7.8 s for a build of main at d5640fee, with reload to open at 1514, 1479 and 1527 ms against 1463, 1564 and 1576 ms and import to open at 1232, 1072 and 1084 ms against 1085, 1086 and 1082 ms; the CI trace shows import to open at 2.34 s and reload to open above 5 s, so the runner was slow and the spec and its timeout are unchanged. Chromium specs with --workers=2 pass after round 8: cad-sketch-arc-trim 1/1, agent-file-import 1/1, cad-sketch-dimension-selection 3/3, cad-sketch-constraints 28/28, cad-sketch-circle-trim 1/1 and cad-sketch-reference-dimensions 1/1; after round 7: cad-sketch-dimension-selection 2/2 and cad-sketch-constraints 28/28; and after the merge with 0.0.779: cad-sketch-dimension-selection 2/2, cad-sketch-constraints 28/28, cad-sketch-reference-dimensions 1/1, cad-sketch-selectable-axes 1/1 and cad-workflow 32/32; the cad-sketch-constraints point editing step now selects Point 2 with Space before Delete, because a refused nudge selects Point 1 and Delete acts on the selection. Round 9: a Chromium test samples 180 places around a dashed construction circle under a radius dimension and finds each answered by the circle or the value label, never the line or arrow targets beneath, and a click at the arrow tip selects the circle and leaves the radius unselected; with the continuous hit stroke reverted, 71 of the samples reach what lies beneath and the test fails. The render test now also checks that a window blur after hovering a line drops its mark and the measured edge highlight, and fails without the blur listener. Chromium specs with --workers=2 pass after round 9: cad-sketch-dimension-selection 4/4, cad-sketch-arc-trim 1/1, cad-sketch-editing 2/2, cad-sketch-midpoint 1/1, cad-sketch-mirror-copy 1/1, cad-sketch-persistent-reference 1/1 and cad-sketch-constraints 28/28. No controller or machine verification applies because output is unchanged.

publicNotes.summary: Sketch dimensions select on click and edit on double-click.
changes: Hover a dimension, or a row in the relations list, to highlight the geometry it measures, including the origin or axis for a coordinate.
Click a dimension to select it, Shift-click to add or remove one and Escape to clear. Double-click or press Enter to edit it.
Opening a dimension's editor keeps the dimension selected, so Delete removes the dimension and never the geometry it measures.

Opening a dimension in the relations list, also from a point's or curve's menu, selects that dimension alone; switching rows moves the selection, and the editor closes when you select something else or open another part.
Keyboard focus never changes the selection: Delete on a focused dimension, point or edge removes what is selected, and the focused item only when nothing is.
Delete or Backspace removes the selected dimensions in one undo step. Right-click a dimension for Edit value…, Make reference or Make driving, and Delete; unavailable commands explain why.
Dimensions draw with thin lines and plain values; reference values show in parentheses in a dimmer colour, and a selected dimension keeps its selection colour while you point at it or focus it.
The size chips on older and plugin profiles draw as plain values like the canvas dimensions and follow the same click, double-click, Delete and right-click rules.

A selection, keyboard focus or open menu stays with its dimension: a dimension replaced by an edit or brought back by undo starts unselected and without focus, a menu closes when the sketch changes, a reference to a line's length stays selected through Trim and Extend, and Make reference keeps a dimension selected when it was stored on a coincident point, unless the same change removes that coincidence.
Point to line distances, also from an arc or circle center, select, edit, convert and delete like the other dimensions, and selecting the origin or an axis replaces a dimension selection.
Dimension highlights show above the defined, conflicting and redundant colours, and fully defined geometry and its dimensions still select and delete.

Where a dimension's line or arrow crosses or ends on a point, edge, the origin or an axis, that geometry, including dashed construction edges along their whole length, keeps the hover, click, right-click, drag and box selection; the dimension's value, and its line away from the geometry, still select it.
publicNotes.compatibility: Sketches keep using existing relation and dimension kinds, so earlier releases open them. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: Double-click a dimension, or press Enter on it, where a single click used to open its editor, and select a dimension, point or edge before deleting it from the keyboard. Automation that finds dimensions by accessible name should use the new names, such as Dimension distance 15 mm, press Enter to edit. While a dimension editor is open, including one opened from the relations list, the agent viewport now reports no selected geometry.
